steps: Client opens an HTTP request for the next event.
Gateway and API hold the request while registering a bounded waiter.
An event completes the waiter, or a deadline returns an empty timeout response.
API releases request resources and sends the response.
Client processes the result and immediately opens the next long poll.

lesson.scenario: A job client receives near-real-time status using bounded HTTP requests that reconnect after events or timeout.

steps.title: Open a bounded poll
steps.narration: The browser opens request lp-881 with a 25-second server wait and 30-second client timeout.

waiter.detail: No work accepted in this phase

worker.detail: No work accepted in this phase

store.detail: No work accepted in this phase

steps.outcome: One ordinary HTTP request represents the wait.
steps.invariant: Every poll has a finite server deadline and resumes from a version checkpoint so reconnects neither miss nor invent status changes.

steps.title: Register event interest
steps.narration: The gateway indexes request lp-881 by job and minimum version without dedicating a worker thread.

worker.detail: No work accepted in this phase

steps.outcome: A status commit can find the waiting request.
steps.invariant: Every poll has a finite server deadline and resumes from a version checkpoint so reconnects neither miss nor invent status changes.

steps.title: Commit a new version
steps.narration: The render worker atomically advances job J-77 from version 12 to 13.
steps.outcome: The durable status changes before clients are notified.
steps.invariant: Every poll has a finite server deadline and resumes from a version checkpoint so reconnects neither miss nor invent status changes.

steps.title: Complete the held response
steps.narration: The waiter wakes lp-881; gateway returns HTTP 200 with ETag v13 and closes the response.
steps.outcome: The client receives the change once per poll.
steps.invariant: Every poll has a finite server deadline and resumes from a version checkpoint so reconnects neither miss nor invent status changes.

steps.title: Reconnect from the checkpoint
steps.narration: The browser immediately opens a new request using last seen version 13; a timeout would return 204 and trigger the same reconnect.
steps.outcome: No update gap exists between polls.
steps.invariant: Every poll has a finite server deadline and resumes from a version checkpoint so reconnects neither miss nor invent status changes.
